subject: Request: KMS/HSM custody, transport & rotation artifacts for SIG review
messages:
From: Jordan Shepard <jordan.shepard@acme-corp.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: KMS/HSM custody and transport evidence for SIG review

Hi Lauren,

We're preparing our SIG review for next week and need to collect vendor evidence around encryption and key management. Can you provide the following artifacts for Redwood's hosted service tier (hosted API) and notes about Dedicated/Private differences where applicable?

- HSM attestation(s) (dates + certs) for any HSM-backed CMKs
- Signed key rotation manifest or rotation logs (last 12 months) with redaction guidance
- Key access matrix / RBAC snapshot showing which roles can perform unwrap/export/schedule-rotation
- Proof of in-transit encryption (TLS versions enforced, cipher suites, any mTLS for private deployments)
- KMS key policies or snapshot of IAM bindings referencing CMKs
- Notes on BYOK options and whether customer-managed keys are supported in hosted vs. private

We'd like these within 5 business days if possible. If there are attachments that are sensitive, S3 or a secure drive link is fine. We may need a brief one-hour call after to clarify a few items.

Thanks,
Jordan Shepard
Security Program Manager
Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Shepard <jordan.shepard@acme-corp.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: KMS/HSM custody and transport evidence for SIG review

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble the set and provide a secure delivery. Quick notes up front:

- Hosted: all customer data at rest is encrypted with HSM-backed CMKs; we enforce TLS 1.2+ (1.3 preferred) for in-transit and disable legacy ciphers.
- Dedicated/Private: customers can opt for BYOK (customer-provided CMKs) and may have mutual TLS options for VPC/private deployments.

I'll hand this over to our security team to collect the artifacts you asked for. Expect a secure S3/drive bundle within 3 business days for the majority of items; anything that requires NDA or additional redaction we'll flag.

Can you confirm your preferred transfer method (secure S3 link vs. shared Drive folder with access expiration)? Also, any specific redaction rules for rotation logs (e.g., are salted key-hashes acceptable)?

I’ve CC'd Evelyn and Vivek to handle the artifacts and signatures.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
From: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00

Following up internally — draft artifact list we will provide to Acme:

1) HSM attestation: hsm_attestation_20260712.pdf (FIPS 140-2 level 3 attestation + vendor cert)
2) Rotation logs: rotation_log_20251001_20261001_redacted.csv (redacted key IDs, salted hashes available)
3) Signed rotation manifest: rotation_manifest_signed.p7s (PKCS#7 signature over rotation manifest)
4) Key policy snapshot + IAM bindings: kms_key_policy_snapshot_20261013.zip
5) Access matrix: key_access_matrix_redwood_2026-10.xlsx (RBAC roles mapped to key operations)
6) Transport proof: short note plus sample TLS handshake captures (no plaintext)

Notes: the rotation log will have internal key identifiers redacted; we can produce salted hashes if Acme signs an NDA covering mapping requests. Some of the BYOK flow artifacts are only applicable to private deployments and would be provided separately.

Vivek — can you confirm we can produce the signed rotation manifest (HSM-signed) and export a time-windowed TLS handshake capture showing TLS1.2/1.3 only?

Evelyn Hart
Sr. Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Oct 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: KMS/HSM custody and transport evidence for SIG review

Confirming — we have generated the requested artifacts and placed them in a short-lived secure bucket and Drive folder. Summary below and files attached to the internal bundle:

- rotation_log_20251001_20261001_redacted.csv (key identifiers redacted, salted-key-hash column included).
- rotation_manifest_signed.p7s (PKCS#7 signature produced by HSM key used for CMK lifecycle operations).
- hsm_attestation_20260712.pdf (HSM vendor attestation + firmware version).
- kms_key_policy_snapshot_20261013.zip (export of key policies and IAM policy snapshots).

Transport note: TLS 1.2 (>=1.2) and TLS 1.3 enforced for all ingress endpoints. Cipher suites limited to AEAD ciphers (e.g., TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256). Mutual TLS is required for Private deployments when the customer enables mTLS; hosted API uses server-side TLS with certificate pinning in our SDK by default.

Rotation cadence: service-level data keys rotated monthly (automated), CMK material rotated per-runbook (annual root KMS rotation; emergency rotation supported and recorded). HSM-backed CMKs are stored in FIPS-validated HSM, rotation manifests are signed by the HSM signing key.

Secure artifact delivery (external):
- S3 (recommended): s3://redwood-secure/acme/rotation_log_20251001_20261001.csv (expires 2026-10-20)
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/secure/acme/hsm_attestation_20260712.pdf (access gated)

I attached the signed manifest and rotation CSV to the internal thread and uploaded the bundle to the links above. If Acme requires the original (non-redacted) rotation mapping we will need a data mapping agreement / NDA addendum describing who is authorized to receive key mappings.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Crypto & Inference Ops — Redwood Inference
